setup.title: Build Night: Assembling an NVIDIA Graphics Card, a Water-Cooled PC, and the First Game
setup.style: Live-action, cinematic product-assembly documentary: clean macro inserts of parts and tools, a bright daytime workshop that turns into a dim, neon-lit gaming room at night.

cast.name: Alex
cast.description: Alex, a man in his late twenties with tousled sandy-blond hair and light stubble, wearing a black T-shirt under a dark-navy canvas work apron, black cargo trousers, and a black anti-static wrist strap on his left wrist.

extras.voice: Alex, speaking in voice-over, a man in his late twenties with a bright, friendly tenor voice, an upbeat pace and a neutral American accent (S1),
extras.music: Relaxed lo-fi hip-hop beat with soft electric piano and vinyl crackle, kept at low volume beneath the narration throughout.
extras.speech: Alex narrates the build in first-person voice-over, like a build-guide video; he is rarely seen speaking on camera.
extras.framing: This is a step-by-step build film. Almost every shot is an object-focused insert of parts, tools and assembly where only the builder's hands, forearms and apron are visible; when the builder himself is shown, use medium or wide framing and never a facial close-up.

shots.prompt:

In the background, tidy pegboards holding precision hand tools, soldering gear, and neatly organized component shelves establish a calm, methodical maker atmosphere, with soft daylight casting gentle shadows across the bright concrete floor.

Alex, a man in his late twenties with tousled sandy-blond hair and light stubble, wears a black T-shirt under a dark-navy canvas work apron, black cargo trousers, and a black anti-static wrist strap on his left wrist. Carrying a heavy stack of component boxes, he steps up and sets them down onto the workbench beside the green mat. He rests his hands near his apron pockets and speaks in voice-over, explaining that he will assemble an NVIDIA graphics card from loose parts and construct a complete water-cooled PC around it. The boxes remain sealed and stacked on the surface by the end of the shot.

The camera remains stationary in a wide establishing shot, keeping the spacious room and workbench dominant while framing Alex as a full-figure presence without any facial close-ups. The white table, the green mat, and the tall stack of boxed components stay clearly visible throughout, anchoring the clean, orderly workspace before any assembly begins.

The hand lifts the nozzle upward and out of frame, leaving the newly soldered chip sitting firmly bonded in place.

The camera maintains an extreme macro close-up angled slightly downward across the circuit board, rendering the silicon substrate, gleaming metallic solder fillets, and textured fiberglass in razor-sharp detail. With a shallow depth of field, the framing stays locked on the chip, smoothly capturing the subtle drop and settling motion without shaking.
